```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
```


## Problem 1

```{r twinsies_function}

repeated_birthdays = function(n=20) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  birthdays_repeated = length(unique(birthdays)) < n
birthdays_repeated
}
```


```{r itteration_twinsies}
birthday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(.x=number_of_people, ~repeated_birthdays(.x))
  )
```


```{r twinsies_plot}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point( color = "red") +
  geom_line( color = "red") +
  labs( x = "Group Size") +
  labs( y = "Probability of a Repeat")
```
These results indicate that as the group size increases the probability of having two members with the same birthday increases. At first this follows a steep increase until around a group of 15, at this point it becomes a steady rise. At a group size of 35 this increase starts leveling off. While not reaching 1, the probability does get close.


## Problem 2

```{r load in}
patient_files =
  tibble(
    files = list.files(path = "./data"),
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    files = str_c("./data/",files)
    ) |> 
  mutate(
  readings_per_week = map(files, read_csv) 
  )|> 
  mutate(
    files = str_remove(files, "./data/"),
    files = str_remove(files, ".csv")
  ) |> 
  rename(arm_subject  = files) |> 
  separate(
    arm_subject, 
    into =c("arm", "subject_id"), 
            sep = "_") |> 
  select(c(arm, subject_id, readings_per_week))
  
  
files_unest = 
  patient_files |> 
  unnest() |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("week"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "measurements"
  )
```


```{r sphagetti plot}
sphaget_plot =
  files_unest |> 
  mutate(
    week = str_replace(week, "week_", ""),
    arm = case_match(
      arm,
      "con" ~ "control",
      "exp" ~ "experiment")
    )|> 
  ggplot(aes(x=week, y = measurements))  +
  geom_line(
    mapping = aes(group = subject_id, color = subject_id)) +
  facet_grid(~arm) +
  labs( x = "Week") +
  labs(y = "Measurements")
sphaget_plot
```

The data shows that while the control arm shows no marked improvement over time, the experiment arm is showing gradual increases in the measurement over the time period.


## Problem 3

```{r initial variables and hypothesis}
#Initial variables
n = 30
sd = 5
mu = 0


alpha = 0.05
conf_level = 1-alpha
#Ho
mu_o = 0

#removing randomness
set.seed(5)
```


```{r normal distribution}
norm_mu_sd = function(n = 30, mu = 0, sd = 5) {
  
  data = tibble(
    x = rnorm(n,mu,sd)
  )

list =
  data |> 
  summarize(
    mu_hat = mean(x),
    obs = list(x)
  )
list
}


```

```{r repetition_norm}
samples = 5000

t_test_rep = function(samples=5000, n=30, mu=0) {
  rep_norm_mu = 
  expand_grid(
    n=30,
    iter = 1:samples
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    estimates = map(n, ~norm_mu_sd(n=.x, mu=mu))
  ) |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  unnest(estimates) 

  t_tests = 
  rep_norm_mu |> 
  mutate(
    t_tests = map(.x=obs, ~t.test(.x, mu=mu_o, conf.level = conf_level))
    ) |> 
  mutate(
    t_tests = map(t_tests, broom::tidy)
  ) |> 
  unnest(t_tests)

t_tests
}


```

```{r repetition_mu}

mus = c(1,2,3,4,5,6)

mu_delta_2 =
  map(.x=mus, ~t_test_rep(mu=.x) |> 
        mutate(mu= .x)) |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  janitor::clean_names()
```


```{r power_plot}
power_plot =
  mu_delta_2 |> 
  group_by(mu) |> 
  summarize(
    power = mean(as.numeric(p_value) < alpha)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = power)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "True Mean",
       y = "Power of The Test")
power_plot
```
 As the size of the effect increases (as the true value of the mean varries more from the null hypothesis) the power of the test increases. As the true mean reaches 4 the power start to level out at a probability of 1 and continues for all further values. 



```{r mu_hat vs mu}

muhat_vs_mu_p = 
  mu_delta_2 |> 
  group_by(mu) |> 
  mutate(
    mu_hat_rej = if_else(p_value < alpha, mu_hat, NA),
    mean_mu_hat_rej = mean( mu_hat_rej, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_mu_hat = mean(mu_hat)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = mu)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_mu_hat, color = "Across All Samples")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_mu_hat, color = "Across All Samples")) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_mu_hat_rej, color = "Across Rejected Nulls")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_mu_hat_rej, color = "Across Rejected Nulls")) +
  labs(x = "True Mean") +
  labs(y = "Observed Means") 
  
muhat_vs_mu_p
```
 
 The sample average of the observed mean across all tests for which the null was rejected does not at first line up with the true mean. However as the mean increases, this approximation closer aligns and matches the true mean. This is because at a lower true mean, there are less rejections, with only extreme points being assessed. However as the true mean diverges more from the null mean (0), the higher number of rejected value brings a more averaged evaluation from the datapoints as to where the true mean lies.
